title: Map the journey, fix what customers feel
subtitle: A 90-minute virtual workshop on customer journey mapping

audience.who: Contoso support and store team leads

constraints: No access to live customer data during the session
executive_summary: In 90 minutes, 16 Contoso team leads learn to map one customer journey, find its pain points with evidence, and leave with one improvement that has an owner and a check date. The session is virtual and hands-on: two breakout exercises take 35 of the 90 minutes. Everything taught comes from the Contoso journey mapping guide (S1).

sources.title: Contoso Outdoor Gear: customer journey mapping guide

objectives.text: Explain the difference between a journey map and a process diagram.
Map one customer journey across the five Contoso stages.
Identify pain points and moments that matter using evidence.
Commit to one improvement with a named owner and a check date.

modules.title: Welcome and goals

key_points.text: A journey map shows one customer goal step by step, from the customer's point of view.
Today you map one journey and leave with one owned improvement.

modules.talk_track: Welcome the group. State the promise: by the end you will have mapped one journey and picked one improvement with an owner. Ask people to post in chat one customer task that frustrates customers today.
modules.setup: Open the deck on slide 1. Have the chat visible. Breakout rooms created but not opened.
modules.fallback: If chat is slow, call on two people by name to share a task.

activities.title: One frustrating customer task
activities.objective: Surface real journeys the group cares about.
instructions: Post one customer task that frustrates customers today.
Read two others and add a reaction to the one you see most often.
activities.expected_output: A list of candidate journeys in chat.
debrief: Which one could we map today with evidence we have?
activities.fallback: If chat is disabled, use the whiteboard sticky notes instead.

modules.title: What a journey map is

key_points.text: A journey map covers one persona and one goal at a time.
A process diagram shows what the company does; a journey map shows what the customer experiences.
Contoso maps journeys in five stages: Discover, Decide, Buy, Use and Get help.
For each step, capture what the customer does, thinks and feels, and the channel.

modules.talk_track: Compare the two illustrative snippets on the discussion slide. A shows company actions; B shows the customer's experience. Walk through the five stages. Stress one persona and one goal per map.
modules.setup: Show this module's key points and discussion slide. No separate example map or poll is needed.
modules.fallback: If screen sharing fails, read the two snippets from the discussion instructions in the facilitator guide.

activities.title: Journey map or process diagram?
activities.objective: Check that everyone can tell the two apart.
instructions: Compare these illustrative snippets for returning a tent bought online.
A: The returns team checks the order, approves the return and issues a label.
B: I find my order on the website, feel unsure about eligibility and ask for help in chat.
Post A or B in chat for the customer's journey, and explain your choice.
materials: Discussion slide with snippets A and B
debrief: Where do teams usually slip back into process thinking?
activities.fallback: If chat fails, read the snippets aloud and ask for verbal votes.

modules.title: Map one journey

key_points.text: Pick one persona and one goal, list the steps in order, then add doing, thinking, feeling and channel.
Groups of four to six work best, with at least one person who talks to customers every week.

modules.talk_track: Explain the exercise in two minutes, open breakout rooms for 20 minutes, then bring everyone back for a short share-back.
modules.setup: Four breakout rooms of four people. One whiteboard per room, prepared with the five stage columns.
modules.fallback: If breakout rooms fail, run the exercise in the main room with one shared map and rotate who adds steps.

activities.title: Map the online returns journey
activities.objective: Produce a first journey map for one persona and one goal.
instructions: Agree the persona and goal: a customer returning a tent bought online.
List the customer's steps in order under the five stages.
For each step add does, thinks, feels and channel.
Mark each step positive, neutral or negative.
materials: Exercise sheet 1 in the participant workbook
activities.expected_output: One map with at least eight steps, each with an emotion marker.
debrief: Which step was hardest to describe from the customer's view?
Where did you disagree, and what evidence would settle it?
activities.fallback: If the whiteboard fails, use the Your work area on exercise sheet 1, labeling each entry with its stage, does, thinks, feels and channel.

modules.title: Break
modules.talk_track: Five-minute break. Keep the maps open.
modules.setup: Show the break slide with the return time.

modules.title: Find pain points and moments that matter

key_points.text: A pain point is a step where the customer is confused, waits, repeats information or gives up.
Use evidence such as support tickets, chat transcripts, store notes and survey comments. Mark steps without evidence as open questions.
A moment that matters changes how the customer feels about Contoso, or what they do next.
In the 2025 pilot, the most common pain point was entering an order number twice (illustrative).

modules.talk_track: Share the pilot story briefly. Define pain points and moments that matter. Send groups back to their maps.
modules.setup: Same breakout rooms and whiteboards. Keep the module's cited key points visible during the briefing.
modules.fallback: Use the cited pilot finding about entering an order number twice as illustrative evidence for that step only. Mark all other unsupported steps as open questions.

activities.title: Circle the pain points
activities.objective: Find the pain points and pick the moment that matters most.
instructions: Circle every negative step on your map.
Use the cited pilot finding about entering an order number twice as illustrative evidence for that step only; mark other circled steps as open questions.
Ask: Does this step change how the customer feels about Contoso? Would fixing it change what the customer does next? Star one step.
materials: Module key points with the illustrative pilot finding
activities.expected_output: Circled pain points with evidence or open questions, and one starred moment that matters.
debrief: Which pain point had the strongest evidence?
Which open question would you check first?
activities.fallback: If time runs short, each group names one pain point and one moment that matters in chat.

modules.title: Commit to one improvement

key_points.text: Common mistakes: mapping the internal process, several personas on one map, opinions instead of evidence, and no owner.
Each improvement needs one named owner and a date to check progress.

modules.talk_track: Recap the common mistakes. Ask each group to commit to one improvement with an owner and a check date. Point to the feedback survey.
modules.setup: Commitment slide with the three fields: improvement, owner, check date.
modules.fallback: If a group cannot agree an owner, the group lead owns it until the check date.

activities.title: One improvement, one owner, one date
activities.objective: Leave with an owned next step.
instructions: Each group posts one improvement, one owner and one check date in chat.
debrief: What will you check on the date you picked?
activities.fallback: If chat is busy, the facilitator reads each group's commitment aloud and records it.

gaps: The guide does not say how long a journey mapping session should take; the 90-minute length comes from the user's intake.
The guide supplies only an illustrative pilot finding, not detailed evidence for every journey step; unsupported steps remain open questions.

pre_read.summary: Read the Contoso journey mapping guide sections on what a journey map is and the five stages.

items.text: Read 'What a journey map is' and 'The five stages'.
Bring one customer task you think frustrates customers.

questions.text: How confident are you that you can map a customer journey now?
Which part of the session was most useful?
What would you change about the session?

follow_up_email.subject: Your journey map and next step
follow_up_email.summary: Thank you for mapping the online returns journey with us. Here is what we covered and the commitments each group made.
points: Every group mapped one journey across the five stages.
Each group picked one improvement with an owner and a check date.
The feedback survey takes three minutes.
